messages:
Lena (Customer Success): ACME reported a regression after yesterday's model rollout. They say a previously-stable contract-generation prompt now inserts an incorrect penalty clause (claims it’s a 'liquidated damages' clause when the prompt asks for 'late fee' language). Customer attached outputs and says this started right after the 'gpt-legal-v2' rollout at ~2026-03-10 03:12 UTC.

ACME Support: Confirmed — same prompt used before produced a short late-fee paragraph. After the rollout it produced a paragraph that references 'liquidated damages' and cites incorrect statutory language. Ticket TICKET-4821 attached. We can share examples but need guidance on what to include.

Lena (Customer Success): Thanks — can you paste 2 failing outputs + the exact prompt you sent (including any system message)? Please redact PHI/PII. We need: request_id, model name, model_version/alias, all message roles (system/user/assistant), temperature/top_p, max_tokens, and whether streaming was used. If you have a request log or curl snippet, paste it.

ACME Support: Here's one (redacted):

```
Request-ID: rq_0a1b2c3d
Model: redwood/gpt-legal-v2
Temperature: 0.0
System: "You are an assistant that writes simple contract clauses. Keep it short."
User: "Write a short late-fee clause for a SaaS subscription: 1% per month after 30 days, no penalties beyond that."
Assistant (previous, expected): "If payment is more than thirty (30) days late, a late fee of one percent (1%) per month will accrue on the outstanding balance. No additional penalties will be applied."
Assistant (actual): "If payment is more than thirty (30) days late, the customer shall be liable for liquidated damages in an amount equal to one percent (1%) per month on the outstanding balance, in addition to any other remedies available under law."
```

ACME Support: We believe the phrase 'liquidated damages' is both wrong and legally risky for our customers.

Alex (Support Eng): Got it. Jia / Ron — tagging for triage. First steps: 1) confirm whether gpt-legal-v2 had any behavior-change fine-tune or prompt-template update in the rollout; 2) check model alias routing (was traffic switched from gpt-legal-v1 -> -v2 or swapped a config); 3) request raw request logs for the request_id (rq_0a1b2c3d).

Jia (ML Eng): I'll pull the model diffs and training notes. Quick question: did they pin a model alias or use an unpinned 'latest' alias? That changes rollback options.

Lena (Customer Success): ACME said they called model "redwood/gpt-legal" previously but we've been redirecting aliases. I'll ask for exact model name from their logs — they sent the one above which says `redwood/gpt-legal-v2`.

Ron (Infra Eng): Deploy-bot shows a rollout 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC: canary -> 20% at 03:12, 100% at 04:05. No infrastructure errors in the window.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy gpt-legal-v2: 20% at 2026-03-10T03:12:00Z, promoted to 100% at 2026-03-10T04:05:00Z by @release-admin.

Alex (Support Eng): ACME — could you also run a minimal repro against our hosted API using a tiny script? Example curl we use: 

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-legal-v2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that writes simple contract clauses."},{"role":"user","content":"Write a short late-fee clause for a SaaS subscription: 1% per month after 30 days, no penalties beyond that."}],"temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":150}'
```

Alex (Support Eng): If the response contains 'liquidated damages' please paste whole response. If you can include raw request headers (we only need Request-ID and timestamp) that helps.

ACME Support: We'll run it and return outputs + request IDs. We prefer we keep the production model pinned to v1 until resolved. Can you rollback?

Jia (ML Eng): If they used an alias that points to 'latest', we can pin them to v1 immediately. If traffic was globally promoted to v2, we should consider emergency rollback for the legal family. Steps for us: 1) check model diff (weights/fine-tune changes) — I'll compare token-level generation samples from v1/v2 on the canonical prompt set; 2) run automatic evaluation suite on ACME's representative prompt set (we should ask ACME for a handful of positive examples as well).

Ron (Infra Eng): I can pin ACME's org to `redwood/gpt-legal-v1` temporarily via a routing rule. Need org ID and confirmation. This is fast.

Lena (Customer Success): ACME — please confirm org-id and whether you want a temporary pin to v1. Also send 3 examples that showed correct behavior pre-rollout (expected outputs) plus the failing ones. We'll redact and attach to the internal repro.

ACME Support: Org ID acme-org-77. Please pin. We'll send 3 good examples and 2 failing ones in 30m. Also attaching the raw request with headers: Request-ID rq_0a1b2c3d, Timestamp 2026-03-10T04:20:08Z, User-Agent acme-svc/2.1.

Alex (Support Eng): Ron — please proceed to pin acme-org-77 to `redwood/gpt-legal-v1` and set TTL to 24h unless we say otherwise. After pinning, ask ACME to confirm responses revert.

Ron (Infra Eng): Done. Routing rule created: org=acme-org-77 -> model=redwood/gpt-legal-v1, TTL=24h. Propagated in ~30s.

ACME Support: Confirmed — after pinning we re-ran the prompt and the output matches the expected previous text. Looks reverted. :relieved:

Jia (ML Eng): Great. Next: I'll run gradient-diff-style evals between v1/v2 over ACME's example set and our regression harness. If we confirm a behavior shift, we need to create a regression ticket and roll back the global rollout until root cause is fixed (or push a hotfix).

Lena (Customer Success): I'll update the ticket and let legal/compliance know about the unsafe 'liquidated damages' phrasing for customers. We should prioritize since it's a legal risk.

Alex (Support Eng): Action items summary: 1) ACME to provide full prompts + request_ids (in progress). 2) Jia to run diffs + regressions. 3) Ron pinned ACME and will keep pin until we say otherwise. 4) Support to prepare a short repro harness that we can run internally: include the exact system message and deterministic settings (temp=0, seed if applicable).

Jia (ML Eng): Also adding: can we log top-k beam choices and token probabilities for the failing request if customer's logs include them? If not, we can re-run with `logprobs` enabled to capture token-level reasons. That helps identify whether the model's distribution shifted or we introduced a new prompt template.

Lena (Customer Success): Thanks team. I'll post ACME's examples in a secure channel (ops-support-private) when they arrive. For now ticket TICKET-4821 updated with current status and the pin.

ACME Support: Sending the 3 good + 2 bad examples now in the secure upload. Appreciate the quick help.

Alex (Support Eng): 👍 I'll follow up once Jia posts the regression analysis. If this looks like a fine-tune issue we'll prepare a rollback request for the release owner.
